items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: I don't think Whiteman would have had a chance to have T. Garden or Biderbecke or any of these guys.

ctx.x: I had some early jazz musicians, when I forget who there were, too.

I had some, there weren't, in the early 1920s, there weren't so many big bands, but what all of them would have some jazz musicians. I wouldn't imagine that if Whiteman had come along in the 30s, say, especially after 35, and everyone's age was at the same time, and I don't think Whiteman would have had a chance to have T. Garden or Biderbecke or any of these guys. They would have more likely have been with bands that were swinging more, playing more, you see. But in those days, this kind of hotel band was the…
So what you had then was a lot of bands with local reputations, territory bands I guess they called them.
